recorded: 2026-10-02, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook, AMD Radeon 8060S, 124 GB unified), Gemma 4 26B-A4B UD-Q4_K_XL
why: The key split gave the full-layer decode walk something to overlap and took it from 58.44 to 19.04 ms per layer at 262144 keys, but it did not change what the walk reads. A one-token block still presents one (query_tile, kv_head, gqa_tile) plane per slice, so each of the 4 GQA tiles reads its own copy of a KV band the 8 query heads sharing it could read once. That is 4.295 GB per layer at 262144 keys where the unique band is 1.074 GB.
what_changed: The query-block shape became a build-time parameter of the same kernel source, and a decode now launches a shape built for it. `kColumns` is `kQueryRows * kGqaHeads` and must be a whole number of WMMA M tiles; `gqa_tiles` is the GQA ratio over `kGqaHeads`. The pair sets both the shared memory the Q tile costs and how many times the KV band is read, and prefill and decode want opposite ends of it.

prefill.why: A 512-row prefill block is 32 query tiles and already presents 256 blocks, so its 4x re-read is not what it waits on and the 32.5 KB Q tile it buys is worth it.

decode.why: A decode block is one query tile against the whole context: blocks to spare and nothing to spend them on but the walk. At 8 GQA heads each band is read exactly once. The second query row is padding that brings the WMMA M tile to 16 columns -- the kernel is bound by the K/V walk, not the arithmetic, so a half-empty M tile costs nothing.

shapes.what_bounded_it: Sixteen rows is what made the GQA shape look impossible: at kQueryRows 16 and kGqaHeads 8 the Q tile alone is 130 KB against a 64 KB budget, and (kColumns * kQStride + kKBatch * kKvStride) * 2 is 146.25 KB. That analysis held the prefill row count fixed for a case that has one query row. At two rows it is 32.5 KB.
shapes.selection: shape_for_tokens: a block of DECODE_SHAPE.query_rows (2) rows or fewer takes the decode shape, anything wider takes the prefill shape. The shapes are separate compiled objects from one source (gemma4_attention_decode_wmma_full.hip includes the prefill .hip with the shape macros defined), so a device that has only run one has only built one.

kernel_ab.protocol: one full layer, tokens=1, identical buffers and arguments in both arms, alternating repetitions, median reported. The arms differ only in the query-block shape; both run the shipped key split.
kernel_ab.output_equivalence: NaN placement equal, and the split-vs-whole delta is bit-for-bit the same as the prefill shape reports (7638 of 8192 bf16 outputs identical, worst element 0.007812 against a 3.719 peak). The shape reads the same K/V and computes the same thing, so the reassociation difference is unchanged.
kernel_ab.achieved_bandwidth: 1.074 GB of logical traffic in 6.24 ms is 172 GB/s against a measured 238.5 GB/s pure-read roofline, so about 38 percent of the traffic-reduction headroom this shape creates is still on the table.

end_to_end_ab.protocol: scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py's frozen prompt chain through hipengine.LLM.generate_detailed with greedy sampling, one process, arms alternated. Both arms run the shipped key split; the only difference is the query-block shape. Each arm is run twice with different max_tokens and differenced, because the prefill is O(context^2) and hides the decode in the wall.
end_to_end_ab.note: 11.0 ms per token saved, against 5 layers x 1.24 ms = 6.2 ms predicted from the kernel A/B. The measured saving is larger than the prediction and this is not explained; it is recorded rather than reconciled. The kernel A/B is the primary evidence.

end_to_end_decode_rate.against_the_split_unit: The same measurement before this change was 39.8 ms per token (25.15 tok/s) with the prefill shape. That pair spans two units and is not the basis for the claim; the 1.315x paired A/B above is.

prefill_is_unchanged.topline: scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py --prompt 512 --output 128 --context 640 --samples 3 --warmup 1 --expect-gpu 8060S: prefill 1250 / 1234 / 1223 tok/s, decode 28.38 / 28.71 / 29.82 tok/s, public wall 4.36 s, path parity True. The recorded topline is 1242 prefill and 28.92 decode.
prefill_is_unchanged.bit_for_bit_check: The prefill shape was gated against the prefill-shape baseline the split unit froze, with --wmma-full-shape prefill --wmma-full-slices 1. kl_mean 0.0, kl_max exactly 0.0, top-1 1.0, 527 rows. The macro indirection changed no arithmetic.
prefill_is_unchanged.why_it_matters: The prefill is the topline, and the shape change is the first thing in this family that could have moved it. It did not.

correctness.gpu_parity: All 24 pre-existing parity tests still pass, including test_one_token_decode_matches_the_strict_decode_kernel, which now exercises the decode shape at four key counts and still matches the strict kernel.
correctness.planner_unit: tests/test_unit_gemma4_attention_wmma_slices.py, 23 cases: shape selection at the boundary, both shapes being a whole number of WMMA tiles, both fitting in shared memory while the sixteen-row eight-head shape does not, the decode shape needing four times the slices of the prefill shape, and the workspace covering every slice of every plane.

teacher_forced_gate.verdict: passed, kl_max 1.22e-3 against a 0.05 limit, top-1 100% with 0 flips

rocprofv3_kernel_trace.why_the_name_carries_the_shape: The device kernel is in an anonymous namespace and the launcher symbol does not appear in a kernel trace, so the kernel name is the only thing that distinguishes the shapes there. Both objects dispatching a kernel of the same name would make "confirm the intended path ran" unanswerable. The combine kernel keeps one name in both objects; it follows its main kernel one-to-one.

not_supplied: the 500-1000 paired-row promotion standard is met in row count (527, evidence_level numerical_rows) but this is a single chain
a 256K end-to-end decode rate: a 256K prefill is 998 s per arm, so the kernel A/B carries 262144 keys and the end-to-end carries 32768

what_is_left.achieved_bandwidth: The decode shape moves the unique band -- 1.074 GB per layer at 262144 keys -- in 6.24 ms, which is 172 GB/s against the 238.5 GB/s pure-read roofline. The redundancy is gone; what remains is that the walk reads 1024 of every 2048 bytes, because a block takes one KV head's row out of a two-head record.
what_is_left.next_lever: The interleave is the remaining 38 percent. A block reads one kv_head's 1024 bytes out of each 2048-byte key record, so consecutive 64-byte sectors are half-used by any single block. That is not a shape problem and would not be fixed by another shape.
